Apple has updated the Apple Store app's privacy policy with terms related to a yet-to-launch virtual shopping assistant. Details below.

Apple is expanding its use of AI in retail

As discovered by MacRumors, the Apple Store app and privacy pages now include a new section titled "Virtual Shopping Assistant," with content as follows:

In other words, the Apple Store app may eventually feature a chatbot that uses user data to provide personalised responses and help users make purchasing decisions.

Apple says personally identifying information will be stripped from chat content before it is shared with unnamed partners that provide assistant responses, which likely means parts of the experience will be powered by third-party models.

Chat history will be retained in the app so users can revisit it at any time, and will also be retained by Apple for business analytics purposes. Users can separately choose whether to allow their conversations to be used to improve the virtual shopping assistant through a new "Chat Improvements" setting.

Wording in Apple's privacy policy suggests the virtual assistant will initially be available in only some countries and regions, likely launching first in English-speaking markets before expanding to more languages and regions.

Today's news comes just months after Apple previously added an AI chatbot to its Sales Coach app, which provides sales and technical resources to Apple's retail partners. Users access the chatbot through an "Ask" tab, and the bot answers questions based on official Apple training materials and documents.

In addition, Bloomberg previously reported that Apple is testing a system called "Live Notes" in select retail stores, which uses AI to record, transcribe, and summarise Genius Bar service sessions so employees can focus on assisting customers without being distracted by note-taking.

For more information about the Apple Store app and privacy, click here.
